## Final browser evidence and comparison limits (2026-10-20)

Complete real-app walkthroughs passed on staging 06f7035, layer1 bfdac29 (r69), layer2 3bb607f (r80), and layer3 8287dc0 (r89). Capture paths/timestamps remain original. Priority Escape was pre-existing on staging and fixed separately in #1453, integrated into this stack. Spot search -> Escape remains pre-existing on staging and is tracked in #1454: the walkthrough records that failed Escape behavior, then closes with a normal pointer click and verifies popup closure/focus. No claim that Spot Escape passed.

Layer2 fixes the genuinely missing first-use phone assistant entry. Its regression E2E fails on the old layer2 build specifically because the mobile launcher is absent, then passes on the current layer2 head. Exactly one header entry is visible per viewport; the desktop tour anchor remains present after runtime loading. The desktop-only optional tour target is absent on phone.

Cold pointer-open comparisons on parent/layer3 both recorded focus outside the list (BODY), with 71 versus 16 mounted rows. The cold pointer check therefore verifies pointer selection/closure rather than assuming keyboard autofocus; keyboard-open End/Enter remains asserted separately. A later pointer reopen after keyboard Escape did return focus on the parent and failed on layer3. Layer3 now hands focus to the arriving collection after overlay restoration; the complete r89 walkthrough passes that later assertion. Its long priority viewport mounted 15 of 71 logical options (72 native form options including the empty form option), height288, without mounting the full row collection. The r85 control was only a parent comparison, not a complete four-head capture or render. Its earlier wrapper PASS text was incorrect.

The r90 six-arm toolbar comparison is NOT six passing tests. All six specs failed. Phone-first staging/parent/candidate runs fail in the shared openTaskById helper, which expects the desktop-only workspace-tab-grid marker. Desktop-resize runs lose or fail to reach the sheet/description surface; parent reproduces the missing-editor assertion. The r89 failure screenshot shows the whole sheet closed, not a visible loading editor. These failures do not isolate a candidate lazy-editor regression and remain an unresolved regression-spec/harness limitation. No timeout or assertion was weakened. Separately, each full walkthrough opens the actual phone description editor and verifies Name remains clickable; desktop description text save/reload/restoration passed. This is functional evidence, not a passing claim for 04-description-phone-toolbar.spec.ts. No product fix is attributed to the comparison.

CI scope: the current staging contents API returns404 for tests/e2e/tasks/04-description-phone-toolbar.spec.ts; this performance-stack-authored spec is not present there. The staging-e2e.yml workflow is opt-in via run-e2e/manual dispatch, not automatic on each staging PR. Its ui-parallel project would collect this task spec if present. Recent staging branch workflow runs failed overall, but no failure of this absent spec can be attributed to them. Thus the six failures are proven only for our private-stack comparison harness against baseline/parent/candidate apps, not a demonstrated staging CI regression.
